prompt_en: A folk-horror photograph of a fictional adult woman returning from an English midwinter orchard wassail, a rural communal custom becoming unsettling at a household threshold. Use the supplied photograph as the face-and-hair appearance reference: her softly rounded facial outline, large dark brown eyes, small straight nose, soft pink lips, chin-length dark brown bob and separated fringe remain recognizable. She has paused on the cottage side of the open door, crouched low after placing the shared wooden cider bowl outside. A raised wooden sill separates a lit interior from the dark exterior; a bowl rests outside the sill. The complete raised oak sill runs across the open doorway between both jambs, its warm inner edge and dark outer edge exposed. The one broad wooden bowl sits wholly beyond its outer edge on the wet exterior stone step, with its base visibly contacting that stone and a narrow visible strip of stone separating it from the sill. Both her hands still cup opposite sides of the same bowl, fingers following its lower curve while its open rim remains visible. Her connected forearms reach forward over the sill; her torso and both bent knees remain inside, supported by her planted feet on the interior floor. She listens toward the bare trees with her face in three-quarter view. A damp wool dress and open knitted cardigan hold the ordinary warmth of someone expected home; a loose strand of hair against her cheek and quiet parted lips give her a restrained, intimate presence. Beyond the door, a near apple branch carries rain-dark ribbons visibly knotted directly around its wood. Two distant torch-bearing figures stand still between the orchard rows. Warm hearth light touches her face, hands and the sill's inside edge; blue winter dusk keeps the exterior bowl, stone contact and nearest ribboned branch legible. Photograph the encounter from an oblique position inside the cottage in a medium-wide view that includes her full crouched posture, both door jambs, the entire sill and the bowl beyond it. The slightly elevated viewpoint lets the viewer inspect the bowl's open rim and the two hand contacts while the waiting orchard remains beside her. The pause holds a practical question: why has the shared bowl been left on the cold side when its carrier is already home? Wet stone, cider and wool retain tactile photographic credibility.
